title: 1INME · Sales Presentation
speakerNotes: Open the sub-deck. Frame it for sales only — fewer slides, sharper focus.

title: Table of contents
speakerNotes: Walk the audience through the sub-deck sections.

title: Appendix · Sales presentation.
description: Section divider for the sales presentation block.
speakerNotes: Shift into the sales pitch. Twenty slides from problem to next step — feel free to skip the proof slides if the buyer is already convinced. Set expectations: this section ends with a concrete CTA.

title: The modern professional drowns in tools.
description: Bio links, scheduler, CRM, vault, analytics — none of them talking to each other.
speakerNotes: Open with the numbers behind the pain. Read the nine-tools stat first, let it sit, then move through cost, usage, and lost hours. The point: this is real money and real time bleeding out today, not a future risk.

title: What fragmentation actually costs.
speakerNotes: Translate the numbers into business cost. Hours, data, brand, revenue — frame each as something the buyer's team will feel this quarter, not abstractly someday. Pause after 'lost revenue' and ask which one stings most.

title: 1INME — the everything platform.
description: Identity, links, AI, productivity, and analytics in one place.
speakerNotes: Pivot to the 1INME answer. Identity, tools, AI, insight — four cards, one platform. Don't list features yet; sell the shape: one home instead of nine browser tabs.

title: Why 1INME, not the next bundle.
speakerNotes: Pre-empt the 'why not just use a bundle?' objection. Native, beautiful, open, fair — these are the four things bundles structurally can't fake. Mention a competitor by name only if the buyer brings them up.

title: ROI of consolidating onto 1INME.
speakerNotes: Make the ROI math obvious: about $1,400 saved annually, six hours back per week, conversion lift, single invoice. Anchor the buyer to a payback window measured in weeks, not quarters.

title: Where the hours come back.
description: Time saved per week by switching to 1INME.
speakerNotes: Walk the time-savings table left to right. Bio maintenance, lead capture, cross-posting, reporting — call out the biggest win for the buyer's role first. Land the seven-hours-per-week footer total.

title: We replaced six tools and shaved a workday off every week. The team finally has one place to live.
description: We replaced six tools and shaved a workday off every week. The team finally has one place to live.
speakerNotes: Read the quote slowly. Pause on 'shaved a workday off every week'. Mention this is a real early-access customer and offer to set up a reference call after this meeting.

title: Loved by early teams across creator, coaching, and agency.
description: Replace these placeholders with real logos and case studies as deals close.
speakerNotes: If logos are still placeholders, acknowledge it and skip ahead. Otherwise, point to the closest analogue to the buyer in the room — same size, same vertical — and offer to introduce them.

title: What customers measure after 90 days.
speakerNotes: Frame these as 90-day expectations, not promises. Six tools removed and a 24% lift in lead-to-close are the lines that move buying committees — repeat them twice.

title: Pricing, at a glance.
description: Pick the plan that matches the team you have today.
speakerNotes: Anchor on Studio first — most teams land here. Free is for evaluation, Pro is for power individuals, Business is for compliance and scale. Call out the 20% annual discount before someone asks.

title: What buyers ask, and how we answer.
description: The four objections we hear most often — and the proof points to handle them.
speakerNotes: Run the four objections proactively. The buyer is already thinking them; saying them out loud builds trust. Keep each answer to one sentence and move on.

title: How 1INME compares.
speakerNotes: Position relative to the specific tool the buyer mentioned in discovery. We're additive to most of these and replacing one or two — be honest about which is which.

title: Built so legal and IT can say yes.
description: Built so legal and IT can say yes.
speakerNotes: This is the slide for IT and legal — slow down here if either is in the room. MFA, SSO, SCIM, audit, SOC 2 trajectory. Offer the evidence pack on request.

title: What buyers see on day one.
description: A single dashboard that proves the value within the first hour.
speakerNotes: Show what the buyer's workspace looks like on day one — not in three months. Live bio page, trained companion, imported pipeline, working funnel. The point: time-to-value is hours.

title: Three buyer outcomes we underwrite.
speakerNotes: Three outcomes we underwrite. Pick the one that matches the buyer's stated goal from discovery and spend most of the slide there. Skim the other two unless asked.

title: What the first 30 days look like.
description: What the first 30 days look like.
speakerNotes: Walk the four-week plan. The point is predictability: by the end of week four the ROI snapshot is in their inbox, not promised vaguely for 'soon'.

title: Where buyers see early proof.
speakerNotes: Customer stories — replace placeholders with the closest real match before sending. Lead each card with the result, then the customer name. If you don't have a story, leave the card off.

title: Our buyer-side guarantees.
speakerNotes: These four risk-removers are designed to make 'yes' the safe answer. 30-day money-back is the headline; mention white-glove migration is included free on Studio and up.

title: Recommended next steps.
speakerNotes: Tell the buyer exactly what happens next. The four-step ladder gives them an easy first 'yes' — start with the 30-minute walkthrough and book it before you leave the call.

title: Sales CTA
speakerNotes: Close. Pick a slot together on screen; don't leave with 'we'll send a calendar link' — that's where deals stall. Capture the email and book the next meeting live.
